title: Google and Samsung launch Gemini smart glasses from $395
summary: Google and Samsung launch Gemini smart glasses starting at 395 dollars
detailed: Google and Samsung have opened pre-orders for Gemini-powered smart glasses from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, with sales starting on 10 December.
Samsung lists Gentle Monster's US range as $449 to $489, depending on the model.

Google and Samsung now have a dated commercial launch for their Gemini glasses, with two established eyewear brands and US prices starting at $395.
sentences: Google and Samsung have opened pre-orders for Gemini-powered smart glasses from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, with sales starting on 10 December.
Warby Parker's collection begins at $395 in the US, while Gentle Monster's starts at $449.
The announcement on Thursday turns a long-previewed wearable project into a product with prices and a firm release date.
Both collections are launching in the United States; Gentle Monster is also bringing its glasses to South Korea.
India is not among the announced launch markets.
Google says the eyewear currently requires a Google account from either the US or South Korea, as well as a compatible phone and an adult account.
The glasses combine a camera, microphones and open-ear speakers, giving Gemini information about what the wearer is looking at.
Google says users can ask about objects, listen to directions from Maps and request spoken translations without taking out a phone.
These are not glasses that place a screen in front of the wearer's eyes.
Their main interface is sound, supported by voice commands and controls on the frame.
A 12-megapixel camera also records photographs and video.
Google says translation supports more than 70 languages.
Calls, messages and music are part of the offer too, with support for services including YouTube Music, Spotify and Apple Music.
The companies describe battery endurance of up to nine hours per charge.
That is a manufacturer claim, not an independent battery-test result, and the quoted duration varies with settings and use.
Warby Parker has three frame styles named Alden, Reid and Wren, with optical and sunglass versions.
Gentle Monster has six frame designs.
Samsung counts 30 variations across the two collections once differences such as lenses, colours and widths are included.
The $395 and $449 figures are starting prices, not a single price for every configuration.
Samsung lists Gentle Monster's US range as $449 to $489, depending on the model.
Google says the frames weigh roughly 41 grams, with variation between models.
A charging case accompanies each pair.
Supported phones include recent Pixels, selected Samsung Galaxy models and compatible iPhones, with software requirements applying.
The launch also puts a camera and an AI assistant into an ordinary-looking accessory.
Google says a recording light indicates when photos or video are being captured, and capture is designed to stop if that light is obstructed or disabled.
According to Google, camera images used by Gemini are excluded from Gemini History, AI-model training and advertising targeting.
It also says the glasses are designed to blur bystanders' faces before those images reach Gemini for processing.
Those are the company's stated protections.
They should not be mistaken for an independent audit of the device or a guarantee that AI visual answers will always be correct.
Google and Samsung now have a dated commercial launch for their Gemini glasses, with two established eyewear brands and US prices starting at $395.
The initial release is limited to the US and South Korea, not India.
Hands-free AI, camera features and claimed battery life will face their next test when customers begin using the finished products.
